newsitem.title: LEBANON: LEBANON ECONOMY MAY GROW FIVE PCT, BANKER SAYS.
newsitem.headline: LEBANON ECONOMY MAY GROW FIVE PCT, BANKER SAYS.

text.p: The head of the Lebanese Banks Association said the economy could improve in the closing months of the year to reach an annual growth rate of 4.5-5 percent instead of an expected three percent.

Francois Bassil, who is also chairman of Byblos Bank, told the association's annual general meeting on Friday the economy had slowed in 1996 but emphasised that an improvement in the closing months could raise the growth rate.
The Lebanese economy grew an estimated seven percent in 1995. Most estimates for 1996 are for four percent growth.
Bassil said bank credits to the private sector totalled $1.1 billion in the first nine months of the year.
Bank credits now totalled $8 billion for the private sector and $6.5 billion for the public sector out of deposits totalling nearly $18 billion, Bassil added.
